articles.summary: SpaceX CEO Elon Musk has warned that a Democratic sweep of the US House of Representatives, Senate and presidency in 2028 could bring major changes to the country’s political system.In a post on X on Thursday, Musk said such an outcome would be “game over for America” and urged voters to support Republican Senate candidates in the November 3 midterm elections.“My biggest concern is that if there is a clean sweep by Democrats of the House, Senate and Presidency in 2028, they will: Make DC and Puerto Rico states to gain a strong majority in the Senate; Open the borders and legalize everyone living in America illegally to cement a permanent majority; Increase the size of the Supreme Court to gain an immediate majority,” Musk said.— elonmusk (@elonmusk) “This would result in America becoming a permanent one-party state and the end of democracy in any meaningful sense of the word,” he said.“All that is needed to ensure this doesn’t happen is 51 Republican senators in 2029. That is why you should vote for Republican senators this election. Other reasons are irrelevant compared to this one,” Musk added.His remarks came as he emerged as the largest individual political donor in US history, having spent more than $442 million on Republican campaigns and political groups ahead of the midterm elections.The Hill reported that Musk contributed an additional $76.8 million to his America PAC over the past month. The contribution took his total spending on the upcoming elections beyond $442 million. America PAC received the funds over about a week in October.Musk had already spent $366 million supporting Republican candidates and groups. He established America PAC during the 2024 election cycle.According to campaign finance filings cited by CBS News, Musk donated $158 million to the Senate Leadership Fund through two contributions in September. The super PAC supports Republican Senate candidates and later transferred the money to a Texas-based political action committee backing Republican Senate candidate Ken Paxton.Musk donated $75 million on September 9 and another $83 million about two weeks later. The contributions accounted for more than half of the Senate Leadership Fund’s receipts in the third quarter, CBS News reported.He also donated $10 million to the pro-Paxton Lone Star Liberty PAC through his trust. In addition, Musk gave $20 million to the Congressional Leadership Fund, $10 million to the Republican Governors Association and $2 million to the Republican Attorneys General Association.The Texas Senate race is among the closely contested contests where Musk has directed his political spending. I have a strong veto. I hope that won't be the case, but if it is, that's happened before… I will — if they're honest elections,” Trump told reporters.The election comes as the administration faces economic concerns and declining approval ratings. articles.title: Trump's grip on Congress may be slipping
articles.summary: Donald Trump's grip on Congress is starting to look a little shaky. Four days before the US midterm elections, major polls show Democrats with a clear national advantage in the fight for the House of Representatives. The Senate remains more competitive, but new CNN polling has put Democrats ahead in several key races that could decide control of the chamber.Also Read| What's at stake for Trump, his opponents and 2028 White House raceRepublicans currently control both chambers of Congress. Democrats need a net gain of three seats in the House and four in the Senate to take control.US Midterm Elections 2026: What do the latest polls reveal?The latest surveys from major news organisations and pollsters show Democrats leading the national congressional ballot by 8 to 10 percentage points.PollField datesDemocratic leadReuters/IpsosOct 22–2653% to 44% — D+9CBS News/YouGovOct 21–2353% to 45% — D+8NPR/PBS News/MaristOct 19–2052% to 44% — D+8CNN/SSRSOct 15–1849% to 39% — D+10ABC News/Washington Post/IpsosOct 9–1352% to 44% — D+8AP-NORCOct 8–1247% to 38% — D+9The latest national poll in this group is the Reuters/Ipsos survey, which interviewed voters through October 26. The AP-NORC, ABC News/Washington Post and CNN national polls were conducted earlier and should not be read as a measure of voter sentiment on October 30.The AP-NORC poll found that 47% of voters wanted Democrats to control the House, compared with 38% who wanted Republicans to remain in charge. The ABC News/Washington Post/Ipsos survey found an even wider preference for Democratic control: 59% wanted the next Congress to act as a check on Trump, while 35% preferred Republicans to support his agenda.Trump's Approval Rating: How are American voters viewing the President?Trump's approval rating is weak across the major surveys. AP-NORC found that 36% voters approved of his job performance, while 64% disapproved. The ABC News/Washington Post/Ipsos poll recorded 33% approval and 66% disapproval.The Reuters/Ipsos poll, conducted most recently, put Trump’s approval at 32%. Only 25% approved of his handling of the economy and 20% approved of his handling of the cost of living.Economic concerns are central to the election. In the AP-NORC poll, 85% of voters called the economy an important issue when deciding how to vote, while 84% said the same about the cost of living.The NPR/PBS News/Marist poll found that 44% of likely voters viewed their congressional vote mainly as a vote against Trump. Only 21% said their vote was mainly in favour of him.CNN polling shows Democratic path to Senate majorityThe Senate remains harder for Democrats because they must win several Republican-leaning states. CNN’s latest battleground polls, released on October 29, showed Democrats ahead in four important Senate races:Texas: James Talarico led Ken Paxton, 49% to 43%.Michigan: Abdul El-Sayed led Mike Rogers, 49% to 42%.Kansas: Adam Hamilton led Republican incumbent Roger Marshall, 49% to 45%.Maine: Troy Jackson led Republican incumbent Susan Collins, 49% to 45%.The Kansas and Maine leads were within the margin of error. The Texas and Michigan results gave Democrats a stronger advantage, although neither race was certain. The CNN results give Democrats a possible route to the four Senate gains they need. But they would still have to perform strongly in other closely contested races, including Alaska, Iowa, Ohio and South Carolina.Republicans have an advantage in the Senate map because several competitive seats are in states Trump carried in 2024. Democrats therefore need to win multiple races where the presidential vote favoured the Republican Party.Also Read| Are educated Republican districts going extinct?House is more favourable to DemocratsCBS News’ latest House model, based on its October 21–23 poll and district-level data, put Democrats on course to win 229 seats. It said Republicans still had a narrow path to retain control.The model also warned that the Democratic lead had not expanded in recent weeks and that voters who were uncertain about voting tended to lean more Republican.That makes turnout critical. Reuters/Ipsos found that 46% of Democrats were very enthusiastic about voting, compared with 30% of Republicans. The NPR/PBS News/Marist poll also found higher overall enthusiasm among Democratic likely voters.Reading the tea leavesThe latest major national polls point to Democratic gains and put the House within the party’s reach. The Senate remains unsettled, but CNN’s newest battleground surveys show Democrats with a possible path to a majority.The numbers do not guarantee a Democratic sweep. The result will depend on turnout, late-deciding voters and whether Democratic candidates can convert narrow leads in Republican-leaning states into victories.

articles.summary:
The IMF on Thursday said the impact of weather events such as the Super El Nino was yet to materialise for India, which remains the engine of growth for the world economy.
The IMF listed lower crop yields, increased food price inflation and its impact on the purchasing power of households in India due to the Super El Nino.
"So these are risks that we see that India faces, but right now those risks have not materialised," IMF Communications Director Julie Kozack told a press conference here.
She said the IMF will reassess India's growth projections in the January World Economic Outlook update after the risks posed by the weather event materialise.
Earlier this month, the IMF raised India's growth forecast for fiscal year 2027 and fiscal year 2028 to 7 per cent, from the 6.4 per cent and 6.7 per cent projections respectively made in July.
